posts.author: Taiga
posts.content:
[Predictions]

Boldbaatar vs. Suzuki
Takaya Suzuki, DEC
This is a really good prospect fight and might be the best prospect vs prospect fight in this whole tournament, its a shame one of them has to be eliminated so early. Takaya Suzuki is one of the best flyweight prospects in the world currently and has improved tremendously over the past year sense he got that 4 second viral knockout. Suzuki has been training at Killcliff and has been living in America for over a year now getting reps with some of the best fighters in the world. I think this fight will be mainly standing but it wouldn't see surprise me too see Boldbaatar mix in grappling but Suzuki's takedown defense and grappling has improved tremendously due to training with Mitch McKee, Nikita Kulshin, and Ansar Khamzaev. He has really nice footwork and he's very fast, able to prevent shots from reaching due to that footwork and speed, rarely being flat footed making him quite elusive. Suzuki carries power that is rare for flyweight and we saw that when he starched a very solid prospect in Figueiredo at Fury, he sets up his shots with nice feints and his counters are lethal, his hands are extremely fast even for flyweights. Boldaatar is a very aggressive athletic fighter who has legitimate power much like Suzuki, he has nice wheel kicks that he uses often, along with knees and leg kicks. He often crashes in and unleashes lots of strikes at once and he can often catch his opponent during these exchanges but also leaving him vulnerable, his defense isn't the greatest. When his opponent is hurt he doesn't stop with the pressure and will very aggressively seek the finish. Suzuki will have the cleaner striking of the two but Boldaatar aggression might cause Suzuki some problems, I think Suzuki will outpoint Boldaatar to a decision but Suzuki catching Boldaatar as he crashes in wouldn't surprise me, on the other hand Boldaatar overwhelming Suzuki early and finding the finish would also not surprise me. Boldaatar had to pull out of a recent Shooto fight where he would of faced Fujita due to a knee injury. Its unknown if that injury was legit or if he will be fighting with this injury or that's its healed. If the rumors of a ACL tear is true than Boldaatar will be fighting on it, think this fight swings in Suzuki's favor tremendously. Think this is a 60/40 fight even without the Boldaatar Injury rumors and if Suzuki can overcome this tough challenge than this tournament is his too lose.

posts.author: AyyLmaonnaise
posts.content:
[Predictions]

Ming vs Tomar
Tomar DEC

This is such a bad main event, the UFC is really all in on pushing Ming. I think she is lucky to be in the ufc and while amazing, that headkick she hit was a once in a lifetime strike; she was down 2 about to be 3-0 and didn’t really have much of anything going, until Feng walked into the kick. She did also land that kick against Seo as well. Other than this kick, Ming doesn’t really have anything. She’s a really bad striker with no power, and her process doesn’t exist either; she just fills the space. Tomar is very bad herself and we all know the track run of Indians in the ufc, but she at least offers something on the feet. Her striking is the epitome of WMMA striking but at least she throws with bad intentions. I thought she lost to Dos Santos in her debut but the judges gave her the fight off of visuals. She was also seconds from a KO over Bannon as well but fumbled it in hilarious fashion. On the feet I think Tomar should be able to win this one; again, her striking is bad but outside of that head kick there’s just nothing about Ming that I like. For all her faults Tomar at least fights with aggression and throws hard, Ming has no power in her hands and is a point fighter. Ming may try to grapple here, so im not sure how that goes. Her grappling is really bad and even though she’s tried to use it in all of her fights, everyone has been able to easily outgrapple her. I am kind of worried here because Tomar has no ground game whatsoever; 4 losses by sub is bad enough but that fumble against Bannon was just next level bad. If she gets taken down it would not shock me in the least if she somehow finds a way to get subbed, but idk if Ming will have much success. Tomar’s ground game is bad but her tdd is passable. I think she just has to avoid getting clinched against the cage since that’s all Ming does and how she sets up her “takedowns”. It is a worry backing Tomar in enemy territory, but I kind of think she should be able to beat this level of competition. Ming got very lucky to even win this tourney; she robbed her way into the finals and then fluked that win over Feng. Then she got outgrappled by Bruna Brasil of all people. This is a big step down in comp for her but I think this favors Tomar. One thing to note is both of these girls would likely be atomweights if it existed in the UFC; neither girl is at their usual size discrepancy here. I think that benefits Tomar more since her technique is bad, she doesn’t have to worry about Ming being able to avoid most of her shots, and it should make her brawling more effective.

Yin vs Batbayar
Batbayar SUB RD 1

I thought Yin got robbed in the semi finals against Tau, so this is actually a pretty decent replacement for Batbayar in the finals. Yin’s fight with Tau was also a crazy war, so I expect him to match the craziness Batbayar brings. I have some questions about Batbayar’s overall game but I really like what he brings. His striking needs work but he hits very hard and is not afraid to let his hands fly. He is also a really solid wrestler, once he gets on top he usually dominates; in the loss to Tumendeberel he was outwrestling him the entire fight before he made a mistake and got subbed. I still don’t know how to feel about that loss but Nyamjargal has some pretty insane hardware so I don’t think it’s bad. Nyamjargal is also winning UFC fights now so the fact Batbayar was doing well against him is good. Yin on the other hand came up short twice on RTU, but I thought he was robbed both times. He loves to brawl but he gets hit a lot and despite the finishes on his record, he doesn’t seem to hit that hard. On the feet I think this is anyone's game since both guys like to meet in the middle and brawl. Batbayar doesn’t have great technique and at the ufc level this will probably be an issue, but he seems pretty durable and he hits very hard. Yin is also really hittable and we’ve seen him lose twice now to lesser competition because of this. His tdd is good on paper but he’s only defended shots from Tau and Sahota, who have terrible wrestling. Batbayar wrestled before mma and it shows, he’s got great technique and seems very strong. He has been very impressive when he gets on top of people, and I don’t think Yin is ready for that. If this gets extended I do worry since Batbayar has never gone the distance. I kind of favor Yin because he’s been in these crazy fights before and has better cardio/striking. That being said, I think the wrestling attack is going to be an issue early. I think he will defend a few takedowns but eventually Batbayar will get on top, and he will be too much.

Dong vs Park
Dong DEC

I’m not interested in taping this one, I just went with Dong because I watched her fight Ming last year and thought it was a robbery. She’s also the A side being in China and the UFC wanting to bring her back. She’s an NPC on the feet but is big for the weight class and her striking does seem okay. I liked her td entries on RTU but her control is terrible. She seems like a good athlete and I know she scored very high on the PI tests as well. I have next to no clue what Park does but off of a quick wiki cap I can see she’s a former atomweight. I assume Dong wins but really could care less.

Feng vs Abdueva
Abdueva DEC

According to Abdueva's manager this and ***uda/Togtonova are the new matchups for 115, although nobody besides him has corroborated this, so idk. Luckily, I already taped ***uda/Feng and saw Abdueva's last fight. I never got the hype on Feng but she was a lot better than I remembered on tape. She's huge for the weight class, super athletic (she was at the top of the PI tests for women), actually a really solid striker, and better grappling than I remembered. The Ming loss is all time bad but she was dominating before that fluke; she also low-key got robbed against Matsuda as well. Abdueva is primarily a wrestler, I kind of want to take Feng as the more complete fighter, but she does struggle with TDD. She did easily reverse Matsuda/Ming but she can be held down, and I worry the Kyrgyz wrestling is a step above what she's used to. Farida is a really good wrestler and has dominated most of her wins via takedowns; her only loss she was winning with control before she got arm barred. Feng is actually pretty good despite her record but I think the wrestling attack will be too much

Togtonova vs ***uda
***uda DEC

I didn't tape Togtonova but I'm assuming she is a wrestler like her teammate Farida. ***uda is actually a really good prospect, my issue with her is that she is thin margins and a midget. She is an atomweight and doesn't separate that well. I don't know what Anelya does but I know she is on the smaller side of 115 which should help ***uda; I think she was going to struggle with the size of Feng pretty badly. If Anelya is a wrestler this is interesting because ***uda is primarily a wrestler herself. Just going with ***uda because she's more proven, but honestly I wasn't impressed with her. She is a good prospect but I kind of worry about her potential because she's very undersized and has had a lot of very competitive fights.

Matsuda vs Bo
Bo DEC

This is a really tricky one to call. Matsuda is the deserved favorite since she is undefeated and has a good resume, but she’s lowkey a weasel. Her two best wins were very close and you could argue she lost both; the Feng fight I thought she won but I thought she definitely lost to ***uda. She looked dominant in her last fight against a girl who looks solid on paper, but it’s worth noting that Tursyn has a massive hole in her defensive wrestling; once you get her down she is cooked. Matsuda dominated when she got on top but that was kind of expected. She was able to outwrestle Feng but did get reversed at times and really had to work for that fight (she was also getting outworked easily on the feet). Against ***uda she lost the majority of the grappling exchanges and imo, got lucky to win that fight anyways. Matsuda has pretty good top control but I do question exactly how good it is, since she’s only been able to outwrestle girls with bad tdd/grappling. On the feet she is not a very good striker, she doesn’t have a ton of power, is small, and fights very defensive. She was losing to Feng pretty easily in the striking and she “beat” ***uda because she did slightly more on the feet but even then, neither girl threw anything of significance. Bo is in a weird spot as she was in ONE jail for a while and is coming off of a loss. The fight itself was really strange though, you could argue Bo won (imo clearly) although due to ONE’s scoring system she lost the most crucial moments of the fight. I thought she took rounds 1-2, not because she impressed but because she just clinched the entire fight and Xiong couldn’t/wouldn’t get out of first gear. In r3 Xiong ended on top from a failed trip and landed gnp/threatened subs which made her win, but in the UFC Bo likely would’ve won that fight; I think it literally came down to that 1 jab Xiong landed in the last few seconds of r2, as that was quite literally the only significant strike anyone landed. Bo is a weird case because she’s honestly got some good skills and has a crazy amount of experience, but she also has some really bad flaws in her grappling. She apparently was a grappler before MMA and you can clearly see she knows what she’s doing, but she makes a lot of mistakes, Her tdd is actually pretty good and she has good offensive wrestling, but she does slip up and concede takedowns at times; I already mentioned how this cost her the Xiong fight, but she lost the Teo fight in similar fashion and even in her wins got taken down too much. It really worries me against Matsuda because she is dangerous on top and one of the better grapplers Bo has faced. That being said, Bo’s tdd/control has looked improved lately. She probably will get taken down here but I think she can get up and possibly reverse position as well. Like I said, I kind of doubt Matsuda’s grappling a little as the two best girls she’s fought have given her issues there. Bo has bad iq (jjust watch the Miura fight for example, easily outwrestling her and defending positions but then gave her arm up), but she can find reversals and has the ability to control Matsuda herself. On the feet, Bo should take this fairly easily. She’s not an exceptional striker but her technique is good and she is powerful. Matsuda is not much of a striker at all and is a bad minute winner on the feet, so Bo should be fine here. I think she wins fairly easily if this stays on the feet, my worry is that her iq is really bad and she will make a mistake and get subbed. She gets put in bad spots a lot and her two most recent losses came from grappling errors. That being said, she has a huge experience advantage here, has enough grappling to at least show resistance to Matsuda, and is close in age to her. I think this will be a close fight but I think the high level experience of Bo, as well as her MMA experience in general will help her out here.

Baluyot vs Uchida
Uchida SUB RD 1

Flyweight is stacked this year so it’s pretty funny they put the two worst guys in the bracket against one another. I actually like Uchida but he still seems super green. He’s been a pro since 16 but he’s yet to fight anyone good and has multiple long gaps on his record. He’s still insanely young but it’s hard to say how much he’s improved because he’s only fought jobbers for the most part. He’s a pretty slick grappler but he still looks like he’s lacking his grown man strength. He looked very solid in his last two fights but they were against bums and he didn’t show anything I hadn’t already seen. His win on RTU was impressive and I did back him there, but the guy he fought is a complete jobber; even then he still took Uchida down and took his back as well. His losses are really bad as well and he’s getting finished in his own discipline which is a pretty bad look imo. I also don’t know if he can strike (I assume not) or has cardio. For all his flaws though, he is getting a complete layup here; Eros is a jobber. It wouldn’t be an RTU season without a can from Indonesia/Phillippines/India and Eros fits that bill perfectly. He is a guard playing bjj nerd with no wrestling and a padded record. You’ll notice he has 6 subs and only 1 is an RNC, the rest are subs from guard. Eros loves a meme heel hook but he is also content to play bjj off of his back. His defensive wrestling doesn’t exist and his offensive wrestling is bad as well; most of the time he shoots from way out and ends up pulling guard. Even in his wins he’s usually getting outwrestled before getting a sub. The one quality guy he fought at ONE easily outwrestled him and was winning easily before he got meme subbed. Not only are heel hooks low level and rarely work against real comp, but Eros has to crank these for like a minute at a time before his opponents tap. Maybe he catches Uchida in some meme sub but I’d be very shocked. I think he will get easy takedowns and sub this can in a round. Uchida isn’t great but he has some legit bjj skills where Eros is a jobber from the Phillipines.

Jiniushiyue vs Oda
Jiniushiyue DEC

Jini is an okay choice to bring back. He’s not very exciting but he is a decent enough fighter and now has the experience of RTU. His losses are to the winners of the last two flyweight brackets, with the most recent one being very competitive. Jini doesn’t wow me anywhere and honestly is pretty boring, but for this level of competition I’d say he’s pretty skilled. He has the common trait we see with a lot of mid tier asian fighters in that he’s a bit of an NPC; he doesn’t really stand out in any way and just kind of cruises in autopilot in his wins. He’s good but doesn’t wow me. Oda is a weird case, his record looks pretty good on paper but his tape was trash. The MD to Suzuki looks good but I thought he clearly lost both rounds. He picked up two good wins in ONE but you watch those and they were 15 minute sniff fests against guys with no grappling. This is how almost all of his fights go, he strikes for a little bit and then immediately looks for the takedowns. I guess his wrestling is solid in comparison to Asian competition, but even then his technique is basic. He only has a double leg that is pretty telegraphed, and he needs to get you up against the cage to get his game going. He just lay n prays on top, I’m honestly not sure he’s even that good of a wrestler, it’s just that most of his opponents can’t wrestle for ****. Jini does have a weakness on bottom but his tdd is very solid and he does all the right things. Oda is going to have to work his ass off to hold Jini down, and he doesn’t have the cardio for that. He gassed in his most recent loss trying too hard for the td and getting outwrestled. He has a very muscular build and slows a lot because he uses a lot of energy to score tds. He looks fine when he’s the hammer but when his opponents show resistance he wilts a little bit. He doesn’t do a ton of damage on top either so against real comp I think it will be difficult to score. On the feet he is cooked. Not even because Jini is that impressive, but Oda is just simply not a good striker. He is very slow and doesn’t even know the basics of striking; he throws singular shots at a time from his hips, and loops everything. He walks forward with his chin in the air and gets touched up a lot. I think Jini should stuff the tds and keep this standing for an easy win.

Boldbaatar vs Suzuki
Suzuki KO RD 1

RTU is perfect for Suzuki; I think he has insane potential but he’s still green so it’s good to build him up. His last win was probably good enough to go straight to dwcs but this will be good experience. I like Boldbaatar as well but he’s not on the same level as Suzuki. Imo Suzuki is the clear winner of this bracket. He has the benefit of training in the US and just recently won the Fury FC title against another prospect, so he has that experience/preparation at the next level that the majority of these guys do not. My main worry with Suzuki (as is with all Japanese strikers) is his ground game. His tdd has looked good every time he’s faced shots, but he hasn’t faced anyone who can really test it. Boldbataar does wrestle in his fights sometimes but im not blown away by it. His entries aren’t great and he doesn’t chain wrestle well either. Suzuki’s first layer tdd seems fine and training in America I expect him to at least improve somewhat in that area. Boldbaatar hasn’t had much success holding people down on the regional scene, so I don’t expect him to do a ton here. He does have a few subs on his record which is worrisome but most of them are guillotines; Suzuki isn’t going to wrestle so this shouldn’t be a problem. On the feet I do like some of what Boldbaatar offers, but I think Suzuki is a clear level ahead of him. Boldbaatar does hit hard and forces a brawl, which is a stark contrast from the patient, counter-heavy style of Suzuki’s. Suzuki hasn’t faced someone who will get in his face and swing bombs at him but at the same time, Boldbaatar does loop his strikes a lot and is very hittable. Suzuki has sharp defense and very good distance management, thusly I expect him to be able to counter Boldbaatar pretty easily. Suzuki picks his shots well and has crazy power for a flyweight. His technical ability is great and I think he will level up training at a top gym. Boldbaatar isn’t bad but I think he is running into a very hard fight here. The majority of this 125 bracket has bad wrestling, I think Suzuki is going to dominate his way to a contract in early 2027; he seems like the goods to me.

Arimoto vs Larcinese
Larcinese KO RD 2

Both of these guys have really good records but I was quite underwhelmed on tape. Arimoto is just kind of an exister to me. He puts stuff out there but isn’t very active nor is he a good minute winner either. The majority of his fights he just ends up cage pushing you, he has some great power but he only ever throws 1-3 strikes at a time. He’s rocked a lot of opponents but will step off the gas and immediately go to cage pushing once he lands; his tape was honestly a really rough watch. He’s very grindy and patient, but not in an interesting way; it’s not like he’s doing anything advanced, he just takes 0 risks and wants the easy way to win. Joe isn’t that impressive to me either. He has some good hardware for the division but I’m not a huge fan of his process and his tape was weirdly kind of bad. He has a huge advantage training and living in AUS (I really hate they do this, it should be only asians allowed), as well as having beat way better opponents, but Joseph has his fair share of flaws. On paper you’d assume he’s a grappler but he’s a striker through and through. Joseph will grapple in his fights but his wrestling is pretty bad and most of the time he ends up striking until he either hurts his opponents or they end up shooting on him. He did show good wrestling in the Janikowski fight, but that guy also has a large hole in his defensive grappling. Joseph is mostly a striker but his minute winning ability is pretty bad himself. He too throws predominantly single shots at a time, and is very hittable. He’s lowkey kind of chinny, I’ve seen him get dropped and hurt many times, and just last fight he had to come back from getting dropped. I think he should be fine here (especially given Arimoto’s lack of killer instinct) but Arimoto does hit hard so you never know. Joseph has really good power for 125 but I’m not a huge fan of his striking process. I do think he does more than Arimoto though; at least Joseph can fight at a high pace and pressures, Arimoto legit looks to clinch every time he lands a clean shot. Joseph’s wreslting is not good despite how the 4 submissions look, but I think he should be fine here. Arimoto is a heavy cage pusher and his wrestling is nothing special; against international comp I don’t see him being that successful. Joseph’s wrestling is poor but his bjj is solid, and I think he should be a step ahead of Arimoto here.

posts.author: Robwett
posts.content:
[Predictions]

Shi vs. Tomar
Ming Shi, DEC
This fight could honestly go either way. Neither of these ladies impress me at all

Yin vs. Batbayar
Namsrai Batbayar, SUB, R1
Yin got robbed against Tau so I'm happy to see him back but I think he loses this. Yin is probably gonna brawl with Batbayar which is exactly what you shouldn't do against Batbayar

Dong vs. Park
Bo Hyun Park, DEC
Dong was lowkey robbed against Ming Shi but that doesn't really matter since both looked horrible. I like how aggressive Park is and she actually seems to hit pretty hard so I'm picking her

Matsuda vs. Meng
Arisa Matsuda, DEC
I'm picking Matsuda because she looked good in her last fight. Bo looks different every fight based on the decisions she makes, she has a win over Chihiro Sawada which is really good but at the same time I doubt she would win a rematch. I honestly have no idea who wins this

Jiniushiyue vs. Oda
Jiniushiyue, DEC
This is kind of a nothingburger matchup. Jiniushiyue is okay but not very exciting and Oda is okay but not very exciting. I'm guessing this fight is gonna start with Oda holding Jiniushiyue down the entire first round before gassing and losing the 2nd and 3rd because he can't get takedowns

Baluyot vs. Uchida
Takeru Uchida, SUB, R1
BJJ nerd vs BJJ nerd matchup with the difference being that Baluyot's entire game is off his back while Uchida has a well rounded game. Should be a easy win for Uchida but I'm not very confident in him winning this tournament

Boldbaatar vs. Suzuki
Takaya Suzuki, TKO, R1
I really like Suzuki, he's young and commited enough to the game that he's training in the US. I think a undefeated brawler like Boldbaatar is a perfect guy for him to knock out with a counter to get some confidence and momentum. Definitely my favorite to win the flyweight tournament

Arimoto vs. Larcinese
Ryoga Arimoto, DEC
I hate watching Arimoto fight, he has the potential to be more but he refuses to commit to anything. Larcinese seems good on paper but I can totally see him falling victim to Arimoto's style of being slightly dangerous into a decision

Abdueva vs. Feng
Farida Abdueva, DEC
Feng is weird because she looks solid at times and she's physical and absolutely massive but she seems to suffer from a severe case of having no fight IQ. She was getting taken down by Matsuda spamming the same takedowns over and over again and wouldn't adapt to it at all. She might be able to outmuscle Abdueva here but I won't pick someone with her decision making

***uda vs. Toktogonova
Machi ***uda, DEC
I've been saying for quite a while that ***uda is probably too small for the UFC and now she's getting her chance of getting there. This is a grappler vs grappler matchup and I think Toktogonova might match ***uda in size. ***uda should win this but I'm really worried how she's gonna look against bigger competition
